title: Subtype Check
statement: Implement `solve(base_accepts, sub_accepts)`. Each flag is 1 or 0 for a particular input. Return `substitutable` when the subclass accepts every input the base accepts, which in this two-flag model means: if the base accepts, the subclass must accept. If the base rejects, the subclass may do either. Return `break` when the base accepts and the subclass rejects.
constraints: A wider subclass is allowed here
hints: The failure is base_accepts == 1 and sub_accepts == 0.
Do not require the flags to be equal.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Liskov substitution says a subclass must accept what callers already pass to the base.

editorial: Liskov substitution says a subclass must accept what callers already pass to the base. Rejecting a positive amount that the base charged is a break. Accepting an extra case the base rejected does not surprise those callers. The flag pair is that test for one input.
